stories.head: AI engines disagree 2x on brand recommendations, study finds
stories.plain: Research from Treyci shows that AI answer engines recommend different brands for the same query roughly twice as often as they agree — a direct warning for marketers investing in GEO. Comscore also begins measuring sponsored ads inside ChatGPT, signalling that AI-answer ad inventory is becoming a trackable, buyable media channel.

stories.head: Beyond A/B testing: reinforcement learning drives perpetual marketing optimization
stories.plain: Eikona CEO Nir Weingarten argues that bandit and reinforcement-learning methods replace periodic A/B tests with continuous optimization — every impression becomes a learning signal. This shifts how marketing teams budget for experimentation and who owns the testing stack, making it directly relevant to anyone buying or building AI-driven campaign tools.

stories.head: 10 Salesforce Winter '27 updates marketers need to know
stories.plain: Salesforce's Winter '27 release brings Agentforce-powered campaign creation and cleaner reporting tools directly into the marketing workflow. Because Salesforce sits at the centre of many MarTech stacks, these changes affect how teams buy, configure, and govern AI-assisted marketing at scale — making this required reading for anyone evaluating or already running the platform.

stories.head: Rapid AI changes mean GEO is a weekly job now
stories.plain: AI-generated answers shift fast enough that brand visibility inside tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity can change week to week. The article argues PR, SEO, and content teams need a shared, ongoing measurement loop — not a quarterly audit — to track which sources get cited and why. It reframes GEO from a one-time tactic into a continuous operational discipline.

stories.head: The terrifying loophole in your autonomous tech stack
stories.plain: When AI agents hand data between systems to run campaigns autonomously, proprietary and personal data can leak at every handoff. The piece maps the specific failure points and proposes governance controls marketers must build before scaling agentic stacks. It is one of the clearest explainers yet on why governance is not optional once agents start acting.

stories.head: SoundHound AI completes acquisition of LivePerson, forming omnichannel conversational AI company
stories.plain: SoundHound AI has formally closed its purchase of LivePerson, combining voice AI with LivePerson's text-based customer engagement platform across WhatsApp, SMS, and phone. The deal reshapes the conversational AI vendor landscape, giving one company control of both voice and messaging channels — directly relevant to anyone buying or building a CEP strategy.

stories.head: Expert Mode: Moving beyond the limits of traditional A/B testing with reinforcement learning
stories.plain: Eikona CEO Nir Weingarten explains how reinforcement learning replaces periodic A/B tests with continuous, self-adjusting optimization — shifting marketing from snapshot experiments to perpetual learning loops. The interview is a clear, jargon-light introduction to why bandits and RL matter for anyone trying to move beyond basic split testing in campaign or personalization decisions.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: The Agentic Enterprise Arrives in Production
body: AI agents are no longer a roadmap item — Docusign is embedding an Agreement Layer directly into every enterprise agent, Globant is shipping a MuleSoft AI Pod to connect agentic workflows across Salesforce, and Contentful is publishing governance questions for marketing leaders navigating the agentic web. The shift is architectural: agents need contracts, integrations, and authority frameworks, not just prompts.

For marketers, this means the stack question is no longer 'which tool?' but 'what can an agent do on my behalf, and who approved it?' Teams that delay building agentic governance frameworks will find agents either blocked by legacy integration debt or running unchecked — both expensive outcomes.

themes.head: AI Governance Gap Becomes a Business Risk
body: Three converging signals make this impossible to ignore: marketers openly admit AI is acting on bad data, a 'terrifying loophole' in autonomous stacks lets agents make consequential decisions without human review, and most teams are failing a basic AI governance test. The liability is no longer theoretical — it lives in every automated campaign and every AI-generated output touching a customer.

The practical decision this forces is a governance audit before expanding AI automation. Hidden ROI costs (compute, error correction, brand repair) routinely dwarf the efficiency gains marketers publicize, meaning the business case for ungoverned AI is often fictional once full costs are counted.
ev: MarTech · Terrifying Loophole in Autonomous Stack

themes.head: GEO & AI Search Visibility Becomes Weekly Operations
body: Generative Engine Optimization is no longer a quarterly SEO refresh — rapid model updates mean brands must monitor and adjust their AI search presence every week. MarTech's analysis shows that what it takes for AI to find, trust, and cite a brand is a distinct discipline from traditional SEO, requiring structured data, authority signals, and proactive entity management. AI SEO Hacker's launch of KPI-guaranteed AI search optimization across 10 industries signals that vendor markets are already commoditizing the service.

The strategic implication: content operations teams need a standing GEO workflow, not a one-time project. OpenAI's audacious claim about future ad revenue confirms that AI-native discovery channels will carry real commercial weight — brands absent from AI results today are building a visibility debt that compounds.
ev: MarTech · GEO Is a Weekly Job
MarTech · What It Takes for AI to Find Your Brand

themes.head: Conversational AI Consolidates into Omnichannel Voice & Chat
body: SoundHound AI's acquisition of LivePerson merges voice and digital chat capabilities into a single omnichannel conversational platform — a clear sign the industry is consolidating around unified conversation layers rather than point solutions. Gupshup's simultaneous launch of a self-serve Voice AI platform extends the same logic to smaller teams, making enterprise-grade voice engagement accessible without custom integration work.

The decision this forces for marketers is channel strategy: siloed chatbot and IVR budgets are increasingly inefficient when customers move fluidly between voice and text. Teams evaluating conversational tools in 2026 should demand a single conversation memory across channels, not separate platforms stitched together post-purchase.
ev: MarTech Series · Gupshup Voice AI Launch

themes.head: Stack Bloat & the Buyer-Seller Speed Gap
body: A sharp new dynamic is emerging: software buyers are adopting and abandoning tools faster than vendors can update their positioning or pricing models. The '16th tool in a 15-tool stack' framing from Kana's Jessica Vose captures the fatigue — marketing teams keep adding AI point solutions without retiring anything, creating integration debt and measurement chaos. Meanwhile, buyers who moved quickly are already demanding replacement, while vendors are still pitching the original feature set.

The governance response is lean-stack discipline: IFPA's example of running a global digital experience with two people by building reusable capability — rather than accumulating tools — is the counter-model. Agile Brand's analysis of moving beyond traditional A/B testing points the same direction: fewer, smarter experiments with AI replacing the need for sprawling toolsets.

month.takeaway: Across every signal this month, the real work has shifted from adopting AI to governing what AI is already doing — in your stack, in your search visibility, in your agents, and in your cost models.
